clues.text: I was a son of Ahimelech.
I escaped when Saul had the priests of Jehovah killed at Nob.
I ran away to follow David after escaping death at the hands of Doeg the Edomite.
I brought an ephod to David when I came to him at Keilah.
I carried the Ark of Jehovah before David during his hardships.
I supported Adonijah when he tried to become king.
Solomon drove me out from serving as priest and sent me to my fields in Anathoth.
David told me to stay with him, saying that whoever sought my life also sought his.
During Absalom's revolt, Zadok and I took the Ark of the true God back to Jerusalem and remained there.
I helped relay Hushai's warning to David through my son Jonathan.
David called me to sanctify myself before the Ark was brought up from Obed-edom's house.
I was the wife of Nabal.
I was discerning and beautiful.
I learned that Nabal had insulted David's messengers.
I quickly loaded bread, wine, sheep, roasted grain, raisins, and figs onto donkeys.
I met David while riding down under cover of a mountain.
I told my servants to go ahead of me, but I did not tell Nabal what I was doing.
I threw myself facedown before David and asked him to let the blame be on me.
I asked David not to pay attention to my husband, whose name meant senselessness.
I told David that Jehovah had held him back from incurring bloodguilt.
When David's servants asked me to become his wife, I offered to wash the feet of his servants.
I rode after David's messengers with five female servants.
I asked David to remember me when Jehovah made him leader over Israel.
David said that my good sense had restrained him from taking revenge with his own hands.
I told Nabal about my meeting with David only after he had become sober.
After my husband died, David sent word to take me as his wife.
I lived with David in Gath as one of his two wives.
The Amalekites carried me off captive when they raided and burned Ziklag.
David rescued me after recovering everything the Amalekites had taken.
I went with David to Hebron after he was directed there by Jehovah.
I bore David a son named Chileab in Hebron.
I told David that Jehovah would hurl away the lives of his enemies as from a sling's pouch.
The Ark of Jehovah was brought to my house on the hill at Kiriath-jearim.
My son Eleazar was sanctified to guard the Ark of Jehovah.
The Ark remained at my house for at least twenty years.
My sons Uzzah and Ahio drove the new wagon that carried the Ark from my house.
My son Uzzah was struck down after he reached out and took hold of the Ark.
I was a Shunammite girl.
I became King David's nurse when he was old.
Although David's servants chose me to lie in his arms and keep him warm, he did not have relations with me.
I was described as extremely beautiful.
Adonijah asked Bath-sheba to request that I become his wife.
Solomon treated Adonijah's request for me as a claim to the kingship.
Adonijah was put to death after requesting that I become his wife.
I was a son of Zeruiah and a brother of Joab.
I went with David into Saul's camp at night.
I offered to pin Saul to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.
I pursued Abner after he killed my brother Asahel.
I called Shimei a dead dog and asked David to let me take off his head.
I helped save David from Ishbi-benob, a Philistine descendant of the Rephaim.
David sent me to chase after Sheba son of Bichri before he could escape into fortified cities.
I chased after Sheba son of Bichri with Joab after he killed Amasa.
I struck down 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
I said that Shimei should be put to death because he had cursed Jehovah's anointed one.
The Ammonites fled from me after they saw the Syrians flee from Joab.
I raised my spear against 300 men and struck them down.
I became head of another three mighty warriors, but I did not attain to the rank of the first three.
I was one of three commanders when David sent his army out against Absalom, alongside Joab and Ittai.
Joab put me in command of the rest of Israel's army while he fought the Syrians.
I told Joab I would rescue him if the Syrians proved too strong for him, and he would rescue me if the Ammonites proved too strong for me.
I was the son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
I was the chief of Saul's army.
I lay asleep near Saul when David entered our camp at night.
David rebuked me for failing to guard Saul and his spear.
I made Ish-bosheth king over Israel after Saul died.
I proposed that young men from my side and David's side engage in combat at Gibeon.
I killed Asahel after he refused to stop chasing me.
I grew angry when Ish-bosheth accused me of relations with Saul's concubine Rizpah.
I urged Joab to stop pursuing my men, warning that the sword would leave bitterness behind.
I promised to turn all Israel to David's side.
I told Paltiel to stop following Michal and return home after she was taken from him.
I spoke with the elders of Israel and Benjamin about making David king.
Joab had me brought back to Hebron and stabbed me in the abdomen.
David said that he and his kingdom were innocent of my blood.
David held a feast for me when I arrived in Hebron with 20 men.
At my funeral, David composed a dirge saying that I had died as a senseless man would.
I was a son of David.
Tamar was my beautiful sister.
I had a daughter named Tamar.
I had no defect from the sole of my foot to the crown of my head.
I cut my hair once a year because it became too heavy for me.
I ordered my attendants to kill Amnon after he had humiliated Tamar.
I fled to Geshur after Amnon was killed and stayed there for three years.
Joab brought me back from Geshur to Jerusalem, but David would not let me see his face.
I lived in Jerusalem for two full years without seeing David's face.
I sent for Joab twice, but he would not come to me.
I ordered my servants to set Joab's barley field on fire.
I told Joab that it would have been better for me to stay in Geshur than to remain unable to see David.
David received me after Joab spoke for me, and he kissed me.
I acquired a chariot, horses, and 50 men to run before me.
I stood at the city gate and stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
I sent spies through Israel to announce that I had become king in Hebron.
I told David that I wanted to fulfill a vow I had made to Jehovah while I was living in Geshur.
I sent for Ahithophel while offering sacrifices at Hebron.
Two hundred men from Jerusalem went with me to Hebron without knowing about my conspiracy.
I had relations with David's concubines on a rooftop before all Israel.
I asked Hushai whether we should follow Ahithophel's advice to pursue David that night.
I and the men of Israel chose Hushai's advice over Ahithophel's.
While David went to Mahanaim, I crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.
I appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab.
My head became entangled in a large tree while I was riding a mule.
Joab drove three spikes through my heart while I was still alive in the tree.
I set up a pillar for myself because I said I had no son to preserve my name.
David mourned for me after I died, wishing that he had died instead of me.
I fled to the court of my maternal grandfather, Talmai king of Geshur.
David commanded his three army chiefs to deal gently with me for his sake.
After I died, my body was thrown into a large pit in the forest and covered with a great heap of stones.
I was king of Gath.
David fled from Saul and came to me.
My servants recognized David as the man celebrated for tens of thousands.
I saw David making marks on doors and letting saliva run down his beard.
I asked why David had been brought to me when I saw that he was acting insane.
I gave David Ziklag after he asked me for a place in the countryside rather than the royal city.
David lived in Philistine territory for a year and four months while he was with me.
I asked David where he had made his raids, and he told me that he had raided the south of Judah, the Jerahmeelites, or the Kenites.
I believed David had become a stench among Israel and would always be my servant.
I told David that he and his men would go out with me and my army.
I told David that I would make him my lifelong bodyguard.
David came to live with me in Gath with 600 men and their households.
After David came to live with me in Gath, Saul stopped searching for him.
David and his men marched at the rear with me when the Philistines assembled at Aphek.
I told Philistine princes that I had found no fault in David from the day he deserted to me.
The Philistine princes made me send David back because they did not trust him in battle.
I told David that he had been as good as an angel of God from my standpoint.
I told David to return in peace and not do anything to displease the Philistine lords.
I ordered David and the servants who came with him to leave as soon as it was light.
I was a son of David and Haggith.
I was born to David after Absalom.
I said that I was going to be king.
I had a chariot, horsemen, and 50 men run before me.
Joab and Abiathar supported me in my bid for kingship.
I held a sacrifice near En-rogel and invited my brothers and the men of Judah.
I did not invite Solomon, Nathan, Benaiah, or David's mighty warriors to my sacrifice.
I became afraid of Solomon and grabbed hold of the horns of the altar.
My father had never corrected me by asking why I had acted as I did.
I asked Solomon to swear that he would not put me to death by the sword.
I told Bath-sheba that the kingship had been mine and all Israel had looked to me, but Jehovah gave it to my brother.
I asked Bath-sheba to request Abishag the Shunammite as my wife.
Solomon treated my request for Abishag as a claim to the kingship.
Benaiah struck me down after Solomon ordered my death.
When I reached David, I bowed facedown and blessed Jehovah for handing over the men who had rebelled against the king.
I was a son of Zadok.
Jonathan and I stayed at En-rogel because we did not dare to be seen entering Jerusalem.
A servant girl brought Jonathan and me a message from Hushai.
Jonathan and I hid in a well at Bahurim when Absalom's servants came looking for us.
Jonathan and I warned David to cross the Jordan because of Ahithophel's advice.
I asked Joab to let me run and take news to David after Absalom's defeat.
I ran by the way of the district of the Jordan and overtook the Cushite.
I told David that Jehovah had freed him from his enemies but said I did not know what had happened to Absalom.
David told Zadok and Abiathar to send everything they heard through Jonathan and me.
The watchman recognized me by the way I ran before I reached David.
I was a priest at Nob.
I trembled when David came to me alone.
I gave David holy bread after he assured me that his young men had kept away from women.
I gave David the sword of Goliath, which was kept behind the ephod.
Doeg the Edomite saw David come to me at Nob.
I told Saul that David was trustworthy, his son-in-law, and honored in Saul's house.
I told Saul that I had not known David was a runaway.
Saul ordered that I and my father's house be put to death.
David told me that the king had sent him on a secret mission.
I told Saul that it was not the first time I had inquired of God for David.
Saul sentenced me and my father's house to death, and Doeg killed 85 priests wearing linen ephods.
My city, Nob, was struck with the sword after Doeg killed me.
My son Abiathar escaped from Nob and ran away to follow David.
I was a son of Ahitub.
After my death, David told my surviving son that he was personally responsible for everyone's death in my father's house.
I was David's adviser.
My advice was esteemed as if someone were inquiring of the true God.
I joined Absalom's conspiracy against David.
I advised Absalom to have relations with David's concubines.
I asked to choose 12,000 men and pursue David that night.
I planned to strike down only David and return all the people to Absalom.
Absalom and the men of Israel chose Hushai's advice instead of my advice.
When I saw that my advice had not been followed, I went home, gave instructions to my household, and hanged myself.
Absalom and the elders initially thought my proposal was right.
David prayed that Jehovah would turn my advice into foolishness.
Jehovah frustrated my sound advice in order to bring disaster on Absalom.
I was from Giloh.
My son Eliam was one of David's mighty warriors.
I was a son of Ithra and Abigail, the sister of Zeruiah.
Absalom put me in charge of his army in place of Joab.
David later appointed me as his army chief in place of Joab.
David told me to gather the men of Judah within three days.
I arrived later than the time David had appointed.
Joab took hold of my beard as if to kiss me and stabbed me in the abdomen.
I was David's nephew and the cousin of Joab, Abishai, and Asahel.
David told Solomon not to let Joab die peacefully after he had shed my blood.
Solomon later had Joab executed after citing the blood he had shed, including my blood.
I was David's firstborn son.
I fell in love with my half sister Tamar.
I became sick with distress over Tamar.
I overpowered and violated Tamar after she pleaded with me not to humiliate her.
My companion Jehonadab advised me to pretend to be sick.
I asked David to send Tamar to prepare food for me.
I refused to eat until everyone had left me alone with Tamar.
I asked Tamar to bake two heart-shaped cakes before my eyes.
The companion who taught me to pretend to be sick was my cousin.
Although a report said that all the king's sons had been killed, I was the only one who died.
My hatred for Tamar became greater than the love I had felt for her.
Absalom ordered his attendants to kill me when my heart was cheerful from wine.
I told my attendant to put Tamar out and lock the door behind her.
After I humiliated Tamar, she lived in isolation at Absalom's house.
I was a son of Zeruiah and a brother of Joab and Abishai.
I was as swift on my feet as a gazelle in the open field.
I chased Abner without turning to the right or the left.
I was counted among David's 30 mighty warriors.
Joab and Abishai killed Abner because he had put me to death at Gibeon.
Abner warned me twice to stop chasing him.
Abner struck me in the abdomen with the butt end of his spear, and I died.
Joab and Abishai pursued Abner after I died.
I was buried in my father's tomb at Bethlehem.
My mother Zeruiah was David's sister, making me David's nephew.
I was a Gileadite from Rogelim.
I was a very wealthy man.
I was eighty years old when David invited me to cross the Jordan with him.
When David fled to Mahanaim during Absalom's rebellion, I supplied him with food.
David asked me to cross over with him, and he would supply me with food in Jerusalem
I asked David to let me die in my own city near the graves of my father and mother.
I sent Chimham with David instead of going myself.
I said I could no longer taste what I ate and drank or hear the voices of men and women singers.
I asked why I should be an added burden to the king in my old age.
David said he would do for Chimham whatever I wished.
David kissed me and blessed me when I was about to return home from escorting him.
Along with Shobi and Machir, I brought beds, pots, grain, flour, honey, butter, sheep, and cheese when David was hungry in the wilderness.
David told his son Solomon to let my sons eat at the royal table because I had helped when he fled from Absalom.
I was the daughter of Eliam.
I was the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
I became pregnant after David lay down with me.
I mourned when Uriah died.
I became David's wife and bore him a son.
Jehovah loved my son and had him named Jedidiah through Nathan.
The son I bore to David became sick after Nathan confronted David.
David comforted me after the child died, and I bore Solomon.
Nathan warned me that Adonijah had become king so that I could save my life and Solomon's.
I reminded David that he had sworn Solomon would sit on his throne.
David renewed that oath to me and ordered Solomon anointed that day.
Adonijah asked me to request Abishag as his wife.
I sat at Solomon's right hand when I brought him Adonijah's request.
I was the son of Jehoiada from Kabzeel.
I was a courageous man who performed many exploits.
I struck down two sons of Ariel of Moab.
I killed a lion in a waterpit on a snowy day.
I took an Egyptian's spear and killed him with it.
David appointed me over his bodyguard.
I did not attain to the rank of the three mighty warriors.
I did not support Adonijah's attempt to become king.
David ordered me to take Solomon on the king's mule to Gihon for his anointing.
I struck Adonijah down after Solomon ordered his death.
I struck Joab down at the altar after he refused to come out.
Solomon appointed me over the army in Joab's place.
I struck Shimei down after Solomon learned that he had gone to Gath.
I was the son of Jesse from Bethlehem.
I was the youngest of Jesse's eight sons.
I shepherded my father's flock.
Samuel anointed me while I was still a young man.
I played the harp for Saul when a bad spirit came upon him.
I became Saul's armor-bearer after he grew fond of me.
I killed Goliath with a sling and a stone.
Jonathan and I made a covenant before Jehovah.
I became king over Judah at Hebron before becoming king over all Israel.
I captured Jerusalem and made it my city.
I brought the Ark of Jehovah to Jerusalem.
Jehovah made a covenant that my royal house and kingdom would last forever.
I showed loyal love to Jonathan's son Mephibosheth and had him eat at my table continually.
I committed adultery with Bath-sheba.
I arranged for Uriah to die in battle.
I comforted Bath-sheba after our child died, and she bore Solomon.
I fled Jerusalem when Absalom rebelled against me.
I wrote many Psalms.
I assembled materials for Jehovah's house because my son Solomon was young and inexperienced.
I arranged for Solomon to be anointed as king before my death.
I told Solomon to be strong, courageous, and obey Jehovah's law after I was about to die.
I was laid to rest with my forefathers.
Paul quoted God as saying that I was agreeable to his heart and would do all the things he desired.
Jesus was called my son.
I killed a lion and a bear while protecting my father's flock.
I refused Saul's armor because I was not used to it.
I told Goliath that I came against him in the name of Jehovah of armies.
I cut off Goliath's head with the Philistine's own sword.
Saul made me a commander over his fighting men because I succeeded wherever he sent me.
The women sang that Saul had struck down his thousands, but I my tens of thousands.
I became Saul's son-in-law after striking down 200 Philistines.
Michal helped me escape through a window when Saul sent men to kill me.
I pretended to be insane before the king of Gath, making marks on the doors and letting saliva run down my beard.
About 400 distressed, indebted, and bitter men gathered to me at the cave of Adullam.
I spared Saul's life in a cave at En-gedi after cutting off the skirt of his sleeveless coat.
I spared Saul again when I took his spear and water jug from beside his head.
After Nabal died, I took Abigail as my wife.
I fled from Saul and lived among the Philistines at Ziklag.
I had the men who claimed to have killed Ish-bosheth executed for murdering a righteous man in his own house.
I danced before Jehovah with all my might when the Ark was brought up.
I wanted to build a house for Jehovah, but he said my offspring would build it.
After the child born to Bath-sheba became sick, I fasted and lay on the ground; when he died, I worshipped Jehovah.
Jehovah loved my son Solomon and had him named Jedidiah through Nathan.
I mourned for Saul and Jonathan in a dirge after they died.
I was called the pleasant one of Israel's songs.
I reigned 40 years, seven in Hebron and 33 in Jerusalem.
I was prevented from building Jehovah's house because I had shed much blood.
I gave Solomon the written architectural plan for Jehovah's temple and its service arrangements.
I was a descendant of Ruth and Boaz through Jesse.
I composed a psalm when Saul sent men to watch my house and put me to death.
I composed a psalm when the Philistines seized me in Gath.
I composed a psalm after the Ziphites told Saul that I was hiding among them.
I composed a psalm when I fled from Absalom my son.
I composed a psalm after Nathan came to me about Bath-sheba.
Stephen said that I asked for the privilege of providing a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
Peter said that I had died and been buried, and that my tomb was still among them.
Saul hurled his spear at me, seeking to pin me to the wall.
Jonathan warned me to hide after Saul spoke openly of killing me.
I asked Jonathan to discover whether Saul's anger toward me had become deadly.
Jonathan and I arranged a signal with arrows to reveal whether I could safely return.
I ate the showbread that Ahimelech gave me at Nob.
Ahimelech gave me Goliath's sword, which had been kept wrapped behind the ephod.
I entrusted my parents to the king of Moab while I was in the stronghold.
Gad told me not to stay in the stronghold but to go into the land of Judah.
When Abiathar fled to me after Nob was struck, I told him I was responsible for the death of his father's house.
After rescuing Keilah from the Philistines, I left because Jehovah said its citizens would hand me over to Saul.
Jonathan came to me at Horesh and strengthened my hand in God.
Abigail restrained me from avenging myself against Nabal and his household.
The Philistine rulers refused to let me fight alongside them at Aphek.
When my men spoke of stoning me at Ziklag, I strengthened myself in Jehovah.
The Amalekites carried off my wives when they raided Ziklag, but I recovered everything.
I made it a regulation that those guarding supplies would share equally with those who went into battle.
I had an Amalekite put to death after he claimed to have finished off Saul.
As a condition of alliance, I required Abner to bring Michal back to me.
I walked behind Abner's bier, fasted until evening, and said a prince and a great man had fallen.
Hiram of Tyre sent cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons to build a house for me.
I inquired of Jehovah twice before fighting the Philistines, and the second time he directed me to circle behind them.
When Uzzah died for taking hold of the Ark, I became afraid and left it at the house of Obed-edom.
When Michal despised me for dancing before the Ark, I told her I would humble myself still more before Jehovah.
I sent messengers to comfort Hanun after his father died, but Hanun humiliated them.
Nathan told me, “You are the man!”
I confessed to Nathan that I had sinned against Jehovah.
After Joab captured Rabbah's water city, I went and took the Ammonite king's crown.
I allowed Absalom to return to Jerusalem, but for two years he did not see my face.
I sent the Ark back to Jerusalem with Zadok and Abiathar when I fled Absalom.
I sent Hushai back to Jerusalem to frustrate Ahithophel's advice.
I ascended the Mount of Olives weeping, with my head covered, as I fled Absalom.
I told Abishai not to kill Shimei when he cursed me during my flight from Jerusalem.
I commanded my commanders to deal gently with Absalom for my sake.
I mourned so intensely for Absalom that Joab warned my servants were ashamed to face me.
I gathered Saul's and Jonathan's bones and buried them in Benjamin after the Gibeonite affair.
I assigned Levites to assist the priests in temple service because the Ark would no longer need to be carried.
Jesse sent me to Saul's camp with roasted grain, bread, and cheeses for my brothers.
I chose five smooth stones from the streambed before facing Goliath.
After killing Goliath, I took his head to Jerusalem and put his armor in my tent.
While living under Achish, I raided other peoples but led him to believe I was raiding Judah.
I sent spoil from the Amalekites to elders in Judah, including places where I and my men had traveled.
I measured Moab with a line, putting two lines to death and one full line to keep alive.
I sent Uriah carrying the letter that ordered his own death.
When I finally received Absalom, I kissed him.
I left ten concubines to care for the house when I fled from my son, and afterward I kept them in a house under guard until the day of their death.
I replaced Joab with Amasa over the army after Absalom's revolt.
Although I swore not to put Shimei to death when he submitted to me, I later told Solomon not to leave him unpunished.
To end a famine, I handed over seven descendants of Saul to the Gibeonites.
After Ishbi-benob tried to kill me in battle, my men swore I would no longer go out with them, so that the lamp of Israel might not be extinguished.
I refused to drink water that three mighty men risked their lives to bring from Bethlehem's well, and I poured it out to Jehovah.
I sinned by numbering Israel and chose to fall into Jehovah's hand rather than man's.
I bought Araunah's threshing floor because I would not offer Jehovah sacrifices that cost me nothing.
I instructed Solomon to deal wisely with Joab because he had killed Abner and Amasa in peacetime.
I gave from my personal treasure for Jehovah's house, and Israel's leaders then offered willingly with me.
I praised Jehovah for making his people willing to offer for the temple and asked him to preserve that inclination in their hearts.
I composed a psalm concerning Doeg the Edomite after he told Saul that I had come to Ahimelech.
I composed a psalm in the cave when I fled from Saul.
Jesus cited my eating the showbread when answering the Pharisees.
Peter said I was a prophet and knew Jehovah had sworn an oath about placing one of my heirs on my throne.
Jesus identified himself as my root and my offspring.
The letter to the Hebrews names me among those who through faith subdued kingdoms.
When Adonijah exalted himself, Bath-sheba and Nathan prompted me to confirm Solomon as king.
I was an Edomite servant of Saul.
I was detained before Jehovah at Nob when David came to Ahimelech.
I told Saul that I had seen David come to Ahimelech at Nob.
I reported that Ahimelech gave David provisions and Goliath's sword.
Saul ordered me to assault the priests after his guards refused to do so.
I was the chief of Saul's shepherds.
I killed 85 priests wearing linen ephods.
I struck Nob, the city of priests, with the sword.
I was present at Nob before Saul ordered the killing of Ahimelech and the other priests.
I was a prophet who lived around the time of David.
I told David not to stay in the stronghold but to go into the land of Judah.
I was called David's visionary.
Jehovah sent me to give David three options after he numbered Israel.
I told David to build an altar to Jehovah on Araunah's threshing floor.
David acted on Jehovah's command that I delivered concerning Araunah's threshing floor.
David chose to fall into Jehovah's hand after I presented him with famine, flight, or pestilence.
The altar I told David to build preceded the end of the scourge against Israel.
I told David to leave the stronghold shortly after he escaped to the cave of Adullam.
I was a Philistine from Gath.
I was a champion of the Philistine army.
I was six cubits and a span tall.
I wore a coat of mail of copper that weighed 5,000 shekels.
My spear shaft was like the beam of loom workers.
I challenged Israel to send one man to fight me.
I taunted the battle line of Israel for 40 days.
I cursed David by my gods and promised to give his flesh to birds and beasts.
David told me that he came against me in the name of Jehovah of armies.
A stone from David's sling sank into my forehead, and I fell facedown.
David cut off my head with my own sword after striking me down.
My sword was wrapped up in a cloth and placed behind an ephod in Nob.
Ahimelech gave David my sword.
I was king of Tyre.
I had always been a friend of David.
I rejoiced when I heard Solomon's words and praised Jehovah for giving David a wise son.
I agreed to provide cedar and juniper timbers for Solomon.
I had my servants make the Lebanon logs into rafts for shipment by sea.
Solomon gave my household wheat and fine olive oil year after year.
Solomon and I made a treaty, and there was peace between us.
I was an Archite and David's friend.
I met David with my robe ripped apart and dirt on my head as he fled Absalom.
David sent me back to Jerusalem to frustrate Ahithophel's advice.
I told Absalom that Ahithophel's advice was not good in that instance.
I advised Absalom to gather all Israel and lead them into battle himself.
Absalom and the men of Israel chose my advice over Ahithophel's.
I warned David through Zadok and Abiathar not to stay at the fords of the wilderness.
I was a son of Saul.
Abner made me king over Israel after Saul died.
I was 40 years old when I became king, and I reigned for two years.
I accused Abner of relations with my father's concubine Rizpah.
I was afraid to answer Abner after he grew angry at my accusation.
I sent for Michal and had her taken from her husband Paltiel.
My courage failed when I heard that Abner had died.
Rechab and Baanah killed me in my bedroom during my midday rest and took my head to David.
I was a Gittite.
I had come from Gath and was a foreigner and an exile.
I told David that wherever he was, whether for death or life, I would be.
I crossed the Kidron Valley with my men and children as David fled Absalom.
David put one third of his army under my command when it went out against Absalom.
David told Joab, Abishai, and me to deal gently with Absalom for his sake.
I was the father of David.
I lived in Bethlehem.
I had eight sons.
Samuel came to my house to anoint one of my sons.
I sent David to the camp with roasted grain, bread, and cheeses.
My three oldest sons followed Saul to war.
Saul accused his servants of siding with my son.
I was a son of Zeruiah, David's sister.
Abishai and Asahel were my brothers.
I was over David's army.
I went up first against the Jebusites after David promised command to the first man to strike them.
I met Abner by the pool of Gibeon, where men from both sides rose up and fought.
After Abner warned that the sword would end in bitterness, I blew the horn and stopped the pursuit.
I confronted David for sending Abner away in peace, saying Abner had come to fool him.
I secretly sent messengers after Abner and brought him back from the cistern of Sirah without David knowing.
I killed Abner in Hebron after he had killed my brother Asahel.
When enemies were positioned in front of me and behind me, I chose Israel's best men to face the Syrians and put Abishai against the Ammonites.
I told Abishai that we would help each other if either battle line proved too strong.
I urged Abishai to be strong for our people and the cities of our God, leaving the outcome to Jehovah.
I sent Uriah into the fiercest fighting after David sent me a letter by Uriah's own hand.
I captured Rabbah's city of waters and called David to finish the capture so the city would not be called by my name.
I saw that David's heart was toward Absalom and sent for a wise woman from Tekoa.
The woman from Tekoa admitted that I had urged her and put words in her mouth.
I brought Absalom back from Geshur to Jerusalem, but David would not let him see his face.
Absalom set my barley field on fire after I twice refused to come to him.
David put one third of the army under my command when we went out against Absalom.
I killed Absalom after David had commanded me, Abishai, and Ittai to deal gently with him.
I rebuked David for mourning Absalom so intensely that his servants felt ashamed after saving him.
I took Amasa by the beard as if to kiss him, then stabbed him in the abdomen.
At Abel of Beth-maacah, a wise woman negotiated with me and Sheba's head was thrown over the wall to me.
I objected when David ordered me to count Israel, but the king's word prevailed.
Adonijah consulted me and Abiathar, and we supported him.
David ordered me and the people with me to tear our garments, wear sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.
I refused to let Ahimaaz carry the first news to David after Absalom died, sending the Cushite instead.
Both Absalom and David moved to put Amasa over the army in my place.
After I killed Amasa, one of my young men called out that whoever favored me and David should follow me.
I did not include Levi and Benjamin in the count because the king's command was detestable to me.
I began the census but did not finish it, and the number was not entered in David's records because wrath came against Israel.
After David lived in the stronghold, I repaired the rest of the city.
At Adonijah's feast, I heard the sound of the horn and asked why the city was in an uproar.
David told Solomon not to let me go down to the Grave in peace because I had killed Abner and Amasa in peacetime.
I followed Adonijah, though I had not followed Absalom, and fled to the tent of Jehovah to hold the horns of the altar.
When Benaiah ordered me to come out from the altar, I said I would die there.
Benaiah struck me down at the altar, and I was buried at my own house in the wilderness.
The man who killed me was appointed over the army in my place.
I loved David as I loved myself.
I made a covenant with the house of David.
I gave David my sleeveless coat, garments, sword, bow, and belt.
I was Saul's son, listed among his sons in Samuel and in Benjamin's genealogy.
I warned David to hide while I spoke with Saul about him.
I told my armor-bearer that nothing could prevent Jehovah from saving by many or by few.
I tasted honey with the tip of my staff because I had not heard my father put the army under oath.
David later looked for someone from Saul's house so he could show loyal love for my sake.
I struck down the Philistine garrison in Geba.
I crossed toward the Philistine outpost with only my armor-bearer, without telling my father.
I treated the Philistines' invitation to come up to them as the sign that Jehovah had given them into Israel's hand.
I climbed up on my hands and feet with my armor-bearer behind me, and we struck down about 20 Philistines.
I said my father had brought trouble on the land after the tired troops told me about his oath.
Saul said I should die for tasting honey, but the people rescued me because I had worked with God that day.
I spoke well of David to Saul, reminding him that David had risked his life and struck down the Philistine.
I asked David never to withdraw loyal love from my house.
At the New Moon meal, I excused David by saying he had gone to Bethlehem for a family sacrifice.
Saul said David threatened my kingship, and then he hurled a spear at me when I asked why David should die.
I left Saul's table in burning anger and did not eat on the second day of the month because David had been humiliated.
I used an arrow signal with a boy in a field to let David know whether he was safe.
I went to David at Horesh, helped him find strength in Jehovah, and said he would become king while I would become second to him.
The Philistines struck me down on Mount Gilboa along with my brothers Abinadab and Malchi-shua.
David mourned me in a dirge and said that my love was more wonderful to him than the love of women.
After news of Saul and me came from Jezreel, my five-year-old son Mephibosheth became crippled as his nurse fled.
Only Saul and I had a sword or spear among the people with us on the day of battle.
The lot singled me out after Saul asked Jehovah to identify the fault between me and the people.
David spared my son Mephibosheth because of the oath between David and me before Jehovah.
Chronicles traces my line through Merib-baal and Micah.
David's dirge said that my bow did not turn back from the slain.
I was a wealthy man of Benjamin.
I was the father of Saul.
I lost donkeys and sent Saul with a servant to find them.
Samuel told Saul that my lost donkeys had been found.
Saul's uncle asked him what the seer had said about my donkeys.
I was the son of Jonathan and the grandson of Saul.
My feet were crippled when I fell as my nurse fled after Saul and Jonathan died.
David restored Saul's land to me and had me eat at his table continually.
I lived in Lo-debar with Machir son of Ammiel.
Ziba told David that I had stayed in Jerusalem hoping for Saul's kingdom to be returned to me.
I told David that Ziba had tricked and slandered me.
I said Ziba could take everything once David had returned in peace.
I was a daughter of King Saul.
I was in love with David.
I became David's wife.
I was Saul's younger daughter.
Merab was my older sister.
Saul gave me to David after David brought Philistine foreskins as a bride price.
I warned David that if he did not escape that night, tomorrow he would be a dead man.
I let David down through a window so he could escape.
Saul later gave me, David's wife, to Palti the son of Laish from Gallim.
Saul meant to give me to David as a snare so that the Philistines might bring David down.
Saul realized that Jehovah was with David and that I loved him.
I placed a teraphim statue on the bed and covered it with a garment.
I put a net of goat hair at the place of the head on the bed.
When Saul's messengers came for David, I said he was sick.
I told Saul that David had said, “Send me away, or I will kill you!”
Ish-bosheth took me from my husband Paltiel and sent me back to David.
From a window I saw King David leaping and dancing before Jehovah as the Ark entered the City of David.
Paltiel walked with me weeping as far as Bahurim when I was taken back to David.
David demanded that Abner bring me before Abner could see his face.
David reminded Ish-bosheth that he had become engaged to me for 100 foreskins of the Philistines.
I began to despise David in my heart when I saw him dancing before Jehovah.
I came out to meet David and mocked him for uncovering himself before the slave girls of his servants.
David answered me that he had celebrated before Jehovah, who chose him rather than my father and all his household.
David told me he would become even more lightly esteemed for celebrating before Jehovah than he already was.
I had no child down to the day of my death.
I was the husband of Abigail.
I was very wealthy; I had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats.
I was harsh and bad in my practices.
I was a man in Maon whose work was in Carmel.
I was a Calebite.
I was shearing my sheep at Carmel when David sent messengers to me.
I screamed insults at David's messengers.
I asked who David was and who the son of Jesse was.
I said that nowadays many servants were breaking away from their masters.
I refused to give my bread, water, and meat for my shearers to men whose origin I did not know.
One of my young men said I was too much of a good-for-nothing fellow to speak to.
I held a feast in my house like the feast of a king.
I was as drunk as could be when Abigail returned from meeting David.
David's men had been a wall around my shepherds by day and by night.
After Abigail told me what she had done, my heart died within me and I became like a stone.
About ten days after my heart died within me, Jehovah struck me and I died.
David said Jehovah had brought my own badness back on my own head.
I was a prophet in the days of David.
Jehovah sent me to confront David after his sin involving Bath-sheba.
I told David, “You are the man!”
I helped make Solomon king in place of Adonijah.
David told me he was dwelling in a house of cedars while the ark of the true God sat among tent cloths.
At first I told David to go and do all that was in his heart, because Jehovah was with him.
Jehovah sent me back to David with the message that it is his offspring that will build a house for His name.
I came to David with a parable about a rich man and a poor man's ewe lamb.
When David said he had sinned against Jehovah, I told him Jehovah had let his sin pass by and he would not die.
I warned Bath-sheba that Adonijah had become king.
I accompanied Zadok when he anointed Solomon as king at Gihon.
I announced that Jehovah would make a house for David.
I told David that his house and kingdom would be secure forever.
In my parable, the poor man's only ewe lamb ate from his morsel and drank from his cup.
David said the man in my parable deserved to die and should repay the ewe lamb four times over.
I told David that Jehovah had anointed him king and given him his master's house and wives.
I declared that the sword would not depart from David's house.
I told David that because he had treated Jehovah with utter disrespect, the child just born to him would die.
Jehovah sent word through me to name Solomon Jedidiah.
Adonijah did not invite me when he sacrificed and claimed the kingship.
I told Bath-sheba that while she was still speaking with David, I would come in and confirm her words.
I asked David whether he himself had said Adonijah would become king after him.
David ordered Zadok, Benaiah, and me to put Solomon on the king's she-mule and take him to Gihon.
I told David that Jehovah had not dwelt in a house from the day He brought Israel out of Egypt, but had walked in a tent and a tabernacle.
I told David that when his offspring did wrong, Jehovah would reprove him with the rod of men.
I said Jehovah's loyal love would not be taken away from David's offspring as it had been from Saul.
I told David that what he had done in secret, Jehovah would do before all Israel and in broad daylight.
After speaking to David, I went to my own house, and Jehovah struck the child so that it became sick.
I bowed with my face to the ground when I came in to speak with King David.
I reported that Adonijah's guests were saying, “Long live King Adonijah!”
The acts of David were written in the words of Samuel the seer, of me the prophet, and of Gad the visionary.
A record attributed to me included the rest of Solomon's acts.
Centuries later, Hezekiah stationed Levite musicians according to the commandment of David, of Gad, and of me; the commandment was from Jehovah through his prophets.
A psalm of David recalls when I came in to him after he had relations with Bath-sheba.
I came to test Solomon with perplexing questions.
I heard the report about Solomon in connection with the name of Jehovah.
I gave Solomon 120 talents of gold, balsam oil, and precious stones.
I arrived in Jerusalem with a very impressive entourage, with camels carrying balsam oil, gold, and precious stones.
I spoke to Solomon about everything that was close to my heart.
Solomon answered all my questions; nothing was too difficult for him to explain to me.
After seeing Solomon's wisdom, his house, his table service, and his burnt sacrifices at Jehovah's house, I was left completely breathless.
I told Solomon I had not put faith in the reports until I saw with my own eyes, and I had not been told the half.
I said happy are Solomon's men and servants who stand before him constantly, listening to his wisdom.
Never again was such a quantity of balsam oil brought in as what I gave King Solomon.
After Solomon gave me whatever I desired and asked for, I returned to my own land with my servants.
I praised Jehovah for putting Solomon on His throne as king for Jehovah his God, because God loves Israel.
Solomon gave me whatever I desired and asked for, more than what I had brought to him.
Jesus called me the queen of the south who came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom.
I was the son of Kish, a Benjaminite, and God gave me as king when Israel demanded a king.
I stood head and shoulders taller than all the people.
Samuel anointed me with oil as leader over Jehovah's inheritance.
The people shouted “Long live the king!” when Samuel presented me at Mizpah.
I rescued Jabesh-gilead from Nahash the Ammonite.
Jehovah rejected me from being king because I rejected his word.
I repeatedly tried to kill David and became his enemy for the rest of my life.
I fell on my own sword on Mount Gilboa after the archers severely wounded me.
My father Kish sent me to look for his lost donkeys, and that journey led me to Samuel.
When Jehovah selected me by lot at Mizpah, I was hiding among the luggage.
The spirit of God empowered me, and I began to prophesy among the prophets.
I cut a pair of bulls into pieces and sent them throughout Israel to summon the people.
I offered up the burnt sacrifice at Gilgal before Samuel arrived, and Samuel said I had acted foolishly.
I spared Agag the king of Amalek alive, along with the best of the flock and herd.
After Jehovah's spirit departed from me, a bad spirit from Jehovah terrorized me.
David played the harp for me and became my armor-bearer.
Women sang that I had struck down my thousands, and David his tens of thousands.
I required 100 Philistine foreskins as the bride price for my daughter Michal.
I ordered Doeg the Edomite to assault the priests of Jehovah at Nob.
I consulted a spirit medium at En-dor after Jehovah would no longer answer me.
Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, my sons, were struck down with me on Mount Gilboa.
I went home to Gibeah after I was presented as king.
When worthless men despised me and brought no gift, I said nothing about it.
I was coming from the field behind the herd when messengers from Jabesh reached Gibeah.
After Jehovah rescued Israel, I refused to put to death the men who had rejected my kingship.
My kingship was reconfirmed before Jehovah at Gilgal.
Samuel said that if I had obeyed, Jehovah would have made my kingdom firm forever, but now it would not last.
On the day of battle, only Jonathan and I had a sword or spear among the people with us.
I put the people under oath not to eat food until evening, until I had taken vengeance on my enemies.
I built an altar to Jehovah; it was the first altar I built to him.
I said Jonathan must die for tasting honey, but the people rescued him.
My wife was Ahinoam the daughter of Ahimaaz.
Abner the son of Ner, my uncle's son, was chief of my army.
I warned the Kenites to leave Amalek because they had shown loyal love to Israel.
After striking Amalek, I went to Carmel and erected a monument for myself.
I grabbed the hem of Samuel's sleeveless coat as he turned to go, and it ripped away.
After confessing I had sinned, I asked Samuel to honor me before the elders of my people.
Samuel did not see me again until the day of his death, for he went into mourning for me.
I hurled a spear at David while he played music, trying to pin him to the wall.
I offered my oldest daughter Merab to David as a snare, but she was given to Adriel the Meholathite.
I gave Michal to David intending her to serve as a snare so the Philistines might strike him.
I sent messengers to watch David's house and kill him in the morning, but Michal let him escape.
At Naioth in Ramah I stripped off my garments and behaved as a prophet before Samuel.
I hurled a spear at Jonathan when he asked why David should die.
I sat under the tamarisk tree at Gibeah with my spear in my hand when Doeg reported on Ahimelech.
In a cave at En-gedi, David cut off the edge of my sleeveless coat but did not kill me.
I wept and told David I knew he would surely rule as king.
While I slept in the camp, David took the spear stuck in the ground next to my head, and the water jug.
I told David I had sinned and acted foolishly after he spared my life again.
I had removed the spirit mediums and the fortune-tellers from the land.
I disguised myself, put on other garments, and went by night to the woman at En-dor.
I was told that the next day I and my sons would be with “Samuel.”
My armor-bearer refused to run me through, so I fell on my sword myself.
The Philistines put my armor in the house of the Ashtoreth images and fastened my corpse to the wall of Beth-shan.
The warriors of Jabesh-gilead took our bodies from Beth-shan, burned them, and buried our bones under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh.
I later gave Michal, who had been David's wife, to Palti son of Laish.
In my zeal for Israel and Judah, I sought to strike down the Gibeonites.
People asked if I was also among the prophets.
When I ate with Samuel, the cook set before me the reserved leg portion among about 30 invited men.
I told my uncle that Samuel had said the donkeys were found, but I did not tell him about the kingship.
God began changing my heart, and all the signs Samuel gave me came true that day.
When I inquired of God about pursuing the Philistines after Jonathan's attack, God did not answer me that day.
I claimed I had carried out Jehovah's word, but Samuel asked about the sound of the flock in his ears.
I said I feared the people and listened to them when I spared what was devoted to destruction.
Three groups of messengers I sent to seize David at Naioth began behaving as prophets, and then so did I.
Chronicles says I died for my unfaithfulness against Jehovah and for consulting a spirit medium instead of inquiring of Jehovah.
The Philistines fastened my skull to the house of Dagon.
David later took my bones and Jonathan's from Jabesh-gilead and buried them in Zela in the tomb of my father Kish.
Paul said that God gave me to Israel as king for 40 years.
I was a Benjaminite, the son of Bichri.
Scripture calls me a troublemaker.
I blew the horn and called Israel away from David.
I shouted that we had no share in David and no inheritance in the son of Jesse.
I told everyone in Israel to go to his gods.
All the men of Israel quit following David to follow me.
The men of Judah stuck to David from the Jordan to Jerusalem when Israel followed me.
David feared I might do more harm than Absalom had done.
David ordered that I be chased so I would not find fortified cities and escape.
Joab's men, the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men left Jerusalem to chase me.
I passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel of Beth-maacah.
The Bichrites gathered together and went in after me.
Joab described me as a man from the mountainous region of Ephraim who had rebelled against King David.
Joab besieged me in Abel of Beth-maacah and raised a siege rampart against the city.
Joab told a wise woman that if the city handed me over, he would withdraw.
The people of Abel of Beth-maacah cut off my head and threw it to Joab.
I was a Benjaminite, the son of Gera, from Bahurim.
I was of the family of Saul's house.
I came out shouting curses at David when he reached Bahurim.
I threw stones at David and at all his servants.
I called David a bloodguilty man and a worthless man.
I said Jehovah had brought back on David all the bloodguilt for the house of Saul.
I said Jehovah was giving the kingship into Absalom's hand.
I walked alongside the mountain abreast of David, shouting curses, throwing stones, and throwing a lot of dust.
Abishai asked to take off my head for cursing King David.
David told his men to leave me alone so that I could curse him.
I hurried down with the men of Judah to meet David when he returned.
A thousand men from Benjamin were with me when I met David at the Jordan.
I fell down before David when he was about to cross the Jordan.
I asked David not to hold me guilty for the wrong I did the day he left Jerusalem.
I confessed that I had sinned and said I was the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet King David.
David swore that I would not die.
David later told Solomon that I had cursed him with a vicious curse on the day he was going to Mahanaim.
David told Solomon that when I met him at the Jordan, he had sworn by Jehovah not to put me to death by the sword.
David told Solomon not to leave me unpunished and to bring my gray hairs down to the Grave with blood.
Solomon ordered me to build a house in Jerusalem and not go out from there to any other place.
Solomon warned that on the day I crossed the Kidron Valley, I would die.
I agreed that Solomon's word was fair and stayed in Jerusalem for many days.
After three years, two of my slaves ran away to Achish the son of Maacah the king of Gath.
I saddled my donkey and went to Gath to find my slaves, then returned with them.
Solomon reminded me that I had been put under oath by Jehovah not to go out to any other place.
Solomon said I knew in my heart all the injury I had done to David.
Benaiah struck me down at Solomon's command, and I died.
I was the son of David and Bath-sheba.
I became king over Israel in place of David my father.
Jehovah appeared to me in a dream at Gibeon and told me to ask for what I wanted.
I asked Jehovah for an obedient heart to judge His people and discern between good and bad.
I ordered a living child cut in two to identify his true mother.
I built the house of Jehovah in Jerusalem.
The queen of Sheba came to test me with perplexing questions.
I was greater than all the other kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
I loved many foreign women besides the daughter of Pharaoh.
In my old age my wives inclined my heart to follow other gods.
I composed 3,000 proverbs, and my songs numbered 1,005.
Jesus said that not even I in all my glory was arrayed as one of the lilies of the field.
Judah and Israel dwelt in security throughout my days, each one under his own vine and under his own fig tree.
I made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt and married his daughter.
Jehovah loved me and sent word through Nathan the prophet to give me a name meaning Beloved of Jehovah.
I rode on King David's mule to Gihon, where Zadok the priest anointed me as king.
When Adonijah grabbed the horns of the altar, I said that if he behaved in a worthy manner not a single hair of his would fall to the ground.
David told me to be strong, prove myself a man, and keep Jehovah's commandments in the Law of Moses.
I rose to meet my mother Bath-sheba, bowed down to her, and had a throne set for her at my right.
I treated Adonijah's request for Abishag the Shunammite as a claim to the kingship.
I sent Benaiah, and he struck Adonijah down.
At Gibeon I offered 1,000 burnt sacrifices on the altar.
I did not ask Jehovah for long life, riches, or the death of my enemies, so He also gave me riches and glory.
My wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the East and all the wisdom of Egypt.
I sent word to Hiram king of Tyre that I intended to build a house for the name of Jehovah.
Hiram and I made a treaty, and there was peace between us.
I spent seven years building Jehovah's house.
I brought the ark of the covenant of Jehovah into the Most Holy of the house I built.
I answered all the queen of Sheba's questions; nothing was too difficult for me to explain to her.
I gave the queen of Sheba whatever she desired and asked for, in addition to what I gave her out of my own generosity.
I made the silver in Jerusalem as plentiful as the stones.
I had 700 wives who were princesses and 300 concubines.
I built a high place to Chemosh on the mountain in front of Jerusalem and to Molech.
The length of my reign in Jerusalem over all Israel was 40 years.
Jehovah said I would be a man of peace and that I would build a house for His name.
David prepared materials for Jehovah's house because I was young and inexperienced.
David gave me the written architectural plan for Jehovah's temple and its service arrangements.
I drove Abiathar out from serving as a priest of Jehovah and sent him to his fields in Anathoth.
When Joab fled to the tent of Jehovah and grabbed the horns of the altar, I ordered Benaiah to strike him down.
I appointed Benaiah over the army in Joab's place and Zadok the priest in place of Abiathar.
I confined Shimei to Jerusalem and later had him struck down after he went to Gath.
I gave Hiram 20,000 cor measures of wheat and 20 cor measures of fine olive oil year after year.
I conscripted 30,000 men for forced labor and sent them to Lebanon in shifts of 10,000 each month.
I built Jehovah's house with prepared quarry stone, so that no hammers or axes or any iron tools were heard while it was being built.
In my dedication prayer I said that the heavens, yes, the heaven of the heavens, cannot contain Jehovah, much less the house I built.
After I finished praying, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices.
Jehovah appeared to me a second time, just as He had appeared to me in Gibeon.
I gave Hiram 20 cities in the land of Galilee, but he was not satisfied with them.
I made a fleet of ships in Ezion-geber, and with Hiram's seamen I brought gold from Ophir.
The weight of the gold that came to me in one year amounted to 666 talents of gold.
I made a great ivory throne overlaid with refined gold, with six steps and lions beside the armrests.
Once every three years my fleet of ships of Tarshish came loaded with gold and silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
I would speak about the trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows on the wall, and about the animals, the birds, the creeping things, and the fish.
I was wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol.
The book of Proverbs opens by identifying me as a son of David and king of Israel.
The Song of Songs is attributed to me.
I brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the City of David to her own house because the places to which the Ark of Jehovah had come were holy.
Jehovah became furious at me because I had inclined away from Him after He had appeared to me twice.
Jehovah told me He would rip the kingdom away from me and give it to one of my servants, but not in my lifetime; one tribe He would give to my son.
When I saw that Jeroboam was a hard worker, I made him overseer over all the compulsory service of the house of Joseph.
I tried to put Jeroboam to death, but he fled to Egypt, to Shishak the king of Egypt.
Nehemiah said that among the many nations there was no king like me, and that I was loved by my God, but foreign wives caused even me to sin.
Jesus said the queen of the south came from the ends of the earth to hear my wisdom, yet something more than me was there.
Matthew records that David became father to me by the wife of Uriah.
I was a daughter of David.
Absalom was my brother.
Amnon, David's son, fell in love with me.
I was a virgin, and Amnon became sick with distress over me.
David sent me to Amnon's house to prepare food for him.
I kneaded dough into cakes before Amnon's eyes and cooked them.
Amnon asked me to bring the food into the bedroom so he could eat from my hand.
When Amnon grabbed me, I pleaded with him not to humiliate me.
When Amnon grabbed me, I told him not to humiliate me, for such a thing is not done in Israel.
I asked Amnon how I could live down my shame.
I urged Amnon to speak to the king my father, saying he would not withhold me from him.
Amnon overpowered me and humiliated me by raping me.
Afterward Amnon's hatred for me became greater than the love he had felt for me.
When Amnon told me to get up and go away, I said sending me away was worse than what he had done with me.
Amnon's attendant led me outside and locked the door behind me.
I was wearing a special robe, the garment that the virgin daughters of King David wore.
I put ashes on my head, ripped apart my fine robe, kept my hands on my head, and walked off crying out.
Absalom told me to keep silent and not let my heart dwell on the matter, because Amnon was my brother.
After Amnon humiliated me, I lived in isolation at Absalom's house.
Absalom hated Amnon because he had humiliated me.
Two years later Absalom's attendants killed Amnon because of what he had done to me.
I was a Hittite.
Bath-sheba was my wife.
I was listed among David's mighty warriors.
David sent for me while Joab's army was besieging Rabbah.
David asked me how Joab, the troops, and the war were getting along.
David told me to go down to my house and relax.
I slept at the entrance of King David's house with the other servants and did not go down to my own house.
When David asked why I had not gone home, I answered that the Ark and Israel and Judah were dwelling in temporary shelters.
I said my lord Joab and the servants of my lord were camping in the open field.
I refused to go into my house to eat and drink and lie down with my wife.
I swore I would not do that thing as surely as David lived.
David told me to stay another day, and I stayed in Jerusalem that day and the following day.
David had me eat and drink with him and got me drunk, but that evening I still slept with the servants and did not go down to my house.
David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by my hand.
David's letter told Joab to put me in the front lines where the fighting was fiercest and then retreat from behind me.
Joab stationed me where he knew there were mighty warriors.
I died among David's servants when the men of the city came out and fought against Joab.
Jehovah later told David through Nathan that he had taken my wife.
Jehovah said David had killed me by the sword of the Ammonites.
My wife mourned me when she heard that I had died.
I was a priest who served with David.
Ahimaaz was my son.
I took the horn of oil out of the tent and anointed Solomon.
I was a son of Ahitub.
I descended from Aaron through Eleazar.
As a mighty and courageous young man, I came to David at Hebron with 22 chiefs from my paternal house.
David called Abiathar and me when the Ark was brought up.
After the Ark came to Jerusalem, I and my fellow priests served before the tabernacle of Jehovah on the high place at Gibeon.
At Gibeon we offered burnt offerings to Jehovah regularly on the altar of burnt offering, morning and evening.
During Absalom's revolt I was there with the Levites carrying the ark of the covenant of the true God.
David told me to take the Ark of the true God back to the city.
David called me a seer and told me to return to the city in peace.
David told me to take my son Ahimaaz and Jonathan the son of Abiathar with me.
Abiathar and I took the Ark of the true God back to Jerusalem and remained there.
David said Hushai must tell Abiathar and me everything he heard from the palace.
Hushai told Abiathar and me Ahithophel's advice and his own advice, and said to warn David quickly.
David sent a message to Abiathar and me to speak to the elders of Judah about bringing him back as king.
Along with Ahimelech from the sons of Ithamar, I helped David make divisions of the priests for their service.
I was listed as leader of Aaron among the tribal leaders under David.
I did not support Adonijah when he tried to become king.
David called Nathan, Benaiah, and me and ordered that Solomon ride on the king's mule down to Gihon.
David said Nathan and I would anoint Solomon as king over Israel at Gihon.
Nathan, Benaiah, the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and I brought Solomon to Gihon on David's mule.
After Solomon became king, he appointed me priest in place of Abiathar.
When Solomon was made king a second time, I was also anointed as priest.
Under Solomon, my son Azariah was listed as the priest among the high officials.
